comments.text: I made the espresso gelato recipe only (without the panna layer) and processed it in the ninja in “gelato”, but it came out quite icy :(. I replace (cause I don’t have) the cellulose for white sugar and dextrose mix, and use slightly less stabilizer mix (LBG, Guar gum, Iota). I feel like using more stabilizers make it gummy. What could be the issue ?
comments.author: @Puflito91

comments.text:
Without the top layer processed through, this isn’t a good coffee recipe. It needed that top layer of fat to be layered throughout. If your use of stabilizers goes gummy, it sounds like you’re not weighing it correctly. 1g too much can make it gummy. 
If you’re looking for just a good coffee recipe, I’m doing one in a few weeks.

comments.text: I'm surprised about you saying that using an espresso machine or pods or a moka pot doesn't matter. There is a metric called Total Dissolved Solids in the world of coffee, it is basically how much solid coffee stuff there is in liquid coffee. For example, if a 40g espresso is 10% TDS, and you dehydrate it, you will find 4 g of dried coffee at the end. Moving on, a by the book espresso from a traditional espresso machine will have a 10% TDS more or less. An espresso coming from a moka pot or a pot machine will have around 3% TDS. That translates into the quantity of ground coffee used for each method. You will use about 15g of ground coffee for 100g of moka pot coffee, or for 100g of Nespresso pod coffee. Whereas making 100g of espresso with a traditional machine will use about 50g of coffee. I'd wager that people using traditional espresso shots wouldn't need the addition of freeze dried coffee at the end.
comments.author: @coffeeandshots

comments.text: Hmm, all that is fine but in the end it's how it tastes to the individual no matter what coffee you use😃
comments.author: @edlondon3717

comments.text: That’s all well and good but to get the additional 30g of pure solids from the instant is actually way more important than increasing the liquid coffee (adding water). If you’re talking solids content, 3% vs 10% in a 100g water solution is almost irrelevant in this recipe.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
I didn't know it was that much. The 30g figure doesn't appear in the list at the beginning and you said a tablespoon. And the what you said made it appear like you were adding instant to achieve a more intense taste than for total solids reasons. 

I personally don't see how 100g of proper espresso wouldn't be enough for 1000g of ice cream, but if it wasn't enough, I would personally look to balance the solids to liquid ratio using different ratio of milk/cream/smp. Admittedly, it's probably easier to tell people to add instant coffee to adjust for the coffee taste rather than rewrite the recipe for different concentrations of coffee. Mostly, I don't really like the taste of freeze dried coffee, a lot of it is robusta, roasted to death, and before the freeze drying process, it's not well brewed.
comments.author: @coffeeandshots

comments.text: @coffeeandshots  that’s the reason my recipes are done, to make it easier for people to make. Encouraging people to reduce coffee to a specific amount to get the right taste strength (for me) is just too complicated for some folk. The point of the channel is to make these recipes as simple as possible whilst giving the a decent result. Also by the time to add any coffee, espresso, freeze dried or whatever, because of the dairy, you’re creating a latte anyway and loosing a high amount of the true flavor.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery
